instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook in batches until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove cooked chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Build the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and sauté until golden brown and softened, about 6-8 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, and 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer Tomato and Cashews
instructions.text: Pour in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add salt to taste, 1 teaspoon honey or sugar, and the soaked cashews (drained). Bring the mixture to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil begins to separate.

instructions.title: Blend for Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until completely smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, if desired.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth sauce to medium heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces, the remaining 1 tablespoon butter, 1/2 cup heavy cream, and 1/2 teaspoon garam masala. Add crushed Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves). Simmer gently for another 8 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot.

tips: For an extra smooth and restaurant-quality sauce, always blend the gravy well and then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes.
Kasoori Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Gently crush it between your palms before adding to release its aroma. Do not skip it!
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors deepen. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to a Timeless Indian Delight

Few dishes evoke the same sense of comfort and culinary delight as Butter Chicken. Known in India as Murgh Makhani, this iconic Indian chicken recipe has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy texture and beautifully balanced flavors. From its humble origins in Delhi to its status as a global favorite, Butter Chicken represents the pinnacle of North Indian cuisine, offering a symphony of tangy tomatoes, fragrant spices, and tender chicken enveloped in a luscious, buttery sauce. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that authentic restaurant experience at home, this comprehensive guide will walk you through every step to master this beloved classic.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter." Its story begins in the 1950s at Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, where Kundan Lal Jaggi, one of the founders, sought to create a way to use leftover tandoor-cooked chicken. He simmered the chicken in a rich tomato-based gravy, fortified with butter and cream, giving birth to a legend.

At its heart, Murgh Makhani features succulent pieces of marinated chicken, traditionally cooked in a tandoor oven, then bathed in a velvety sauce. This sauce is a masterpiece of flavor, combining pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a blend of aromatic spices like garam masala, turmeric, and Kashmiri red chili powder. The addition of cashews provides a natural thickness and sweetness, while fresh cream and a generous amount of butter contribute to its signature richness and smooth texture. The final flourish of dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) adds an unmistakable depth, making every bite of this Butter Chicken dish truly unforgettable. It’s a dish that balances sweetness, tanginess, and a subtle warmth, making it approachable for all palates, even those sensitive to heat.

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components, divided into the chicken marinade and the rich makhani sauce.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   **Chicken:** 1.5 lbs (about 680g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces. Thighs are recommended for tenderness.
*   **Plain Yogurt:** 1/2 cup, full-fat for best results.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Kashmiri Red Chili Powder:** 1 teaspoon (for color, mild heat).
*   **Turmeric Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon.
*   **Garam Masala:** 1/2 teaspoon.
*   **Salt:** 1/2 teaspoon, or to taste.

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   **Unsalted Butter:** 4 tablespoons (1/2 stick).
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Canned Crushed Tomatoes:** 1 (28-ounce) can, or 4-5 fresh large tomatoes, blanched, peeled, and pureed.
*   **Cashews:** 1/4 cup, soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes, then drained.
*   **Kashmiri Red Chili Powder:** 1 tablespoon (adjust to preferred heat and color).
*   **Coriander Powder:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Cumin Powder:** 1/2 teaspoon.
*   **Garam Masala:** 1 teaspoon.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** 1 tablespoon, crushed between your palms.
*   **Heavy Cream:** 1/2 cup.
*   **Sugar:** 1-2 teaspoons, or to taste (balances acidity of tomatoes).
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Water or Chicken Broth:** 1/2 to 1 cup, as needed for consistency.

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped.
*   A swirl of heavy cream.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create your own restaurant-quality Butter Chicken:

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients (yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, and salt). Mix well, ensuring every piece of chicken is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear the chicken for 3-4 minutes per side, until lightly charred and cooked through. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked at this stage, as it will finish cooking in the sauce. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Makhani Sauce Base**
In the same pan (add a little more butter if needed), melt 3 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Mix well and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have cooked down and the oil begins to separate from the mixture.
Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky, restaurant-style sauce, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard any remaining pulp.

**Step 4: Finish the Sauce and Combine**
Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add water or chicken broth, about 1/2 to 1 cup, to achieve your desired consistency. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces.
Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, heavy cream, sugar, and garam masala. Gently crush the kasoori methi between your palms and add it to the sauce. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking in the rich sauce. Taste and adjust salt and sugar as needed.

**Step 5: Garnish and Serve**
Ladle the warm Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of heavy cream. Serve immediately.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

*   **Marination is Key:** The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** Don't skip this. It provides that beautiful orange-red color without excessive heat. If unavailable, use a mix of regular chili powder and paprika.
*   **Blend and Strain:** For an ultra-smooth, restaurant-quality sauce, blending the base until completely smooth and then straining it through a fine-mesh sieve is crucial. It removes any fibrous bits from the tomatoes and onions.
*   **Cashews for Creaminess:** Cashews are essential for the sauce's characteristic richness and thickness. Soak them in hot water first to soften them for easier blending.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is the secret ingredient for authentic Murgh Makhani flavor. Lightly toast it in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing and adding to enhance its aroma.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste your sauce! Adjust salt, sugar, and even a touch more lemon juice or cream to achieve the perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and savory.
*   **Don't Overcook the Chicken:** Sear it until lightly cooked, then let it finish simmering in the sauce to keep it moist and tender.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken is incredibly versatile and pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice dishes.
*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy naan is perfect for soaking up every drop of the luxurious sauce. Garlic naan or butter naan are excellent choices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed plain basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a light contrast to the rich curry.
*   **Roti or Paratha:** Other Indian flatbreads like whole wheat roti or flaky paratha also make great accompaniments.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) can offer a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the Butter Chicken.
*   **Simple Salad:** A side of sliced red onion, cucumber, and tomato can add freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic recipe is a masterpiece, you can easily adapt Butter Chicken to suit different dietary needs or preferences:
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables like cauliflower and peas for Paneer Makhani or Vegetable Makhani. For a vegan version, use coconut cream instead of dairy cream, and a plant-based butter alternative.
*   **Chicken Type:** While boneless thighs are recommended for their tenderness, chicken breasts work well too.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder. For more heat, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or finely chopped green chilies.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you want a tandoor-like smoky flavor without a tandoor, you can use the "dhungar" method: place a small bowl with a hot piece of charcoal in the center of the finished curry, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for 5-10 minutes to infuse with smoke.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: What is the difference between Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala?**
A: While both are popular creamy chicken curries, Butter Chicken is generally sweeter, milder, and has a smoother, richer tomato-cream sauce. Chicken Tikka Masala often features more prominent spices, a tangier sauce, and sometimes includes bell peppers and onions, offering a spicier and more robust flavor profile.

**Q: Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?**
A: Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It also freezes well for up to 3 months.

**Q: Is Butter Chicken spicy?**
A: Traditionally, Butter Chicken is a mild to medium-spiced dish, relying more on aroma and richness than intense heat. The Kashmiri red chili powder contributes color and a gentle warmth, but you can easily adjust the amount to suit your preference.

**Q: Do I have to use cashews?**
A: Cashews are highly recommended as they contribute significantly to the sauce's creamy texture and subtle sweetness. If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute with blanched almonds or use a small amount of cornstarch slurry (cornstarch mixed with water) to thicken the sauce, though the flavor profile will be slightly different.

**Q: What is Kasoori Methi?**
A: Kasoori Methi refers to dried fenugreek leaves. They have a unique, slightly bitter, yet aromatic flavor that is quintessential to many North Indian dishes, including Butter Chicken. It's often found in Indian grocery stores.

Embrace the joy of cooking this classic Indian dish. With this detailed recipe and helpful tips, you’re well on your way to mastering the art of Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani, bringing the authentic flavors of India right into your kitchen. Enjoy!
